chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'By My Honour, and My Majesty, and My Magnificence, and My Greatness, and My Light, and My Exaltedness, and the Loftiness of My Position! A servant would not prefer his own personal desires over My Desires except that I scatter his affairs over him, and confuse his world for him, and occupy his heart with it, and would not give him from it except what I have ordained for him. And by My Honour, and My Majesty, and My Magnificence, and My Light, and My Exaltedness, and the Loftiness of My Position! No servant would prefer My Desires above his own personal desires except that I make My Angels guard him, and the skies and the earth would guarantee his sustenance, and I would back him from behind every trade with every trader, and the world would come to him and it (world) would be subdued.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference in divine reward between preferring one's own desires versus God's desires?
ai.summary: This Hadith Qudsi, recorded in Al-Kafi, illustrates the metaphysical mechanics of divine reciprocity where prioritizing God's will over self-interest triggers a cosmic guarantee of sustenance (rizq) and angelic protection. It serves as a cornerstone for the Shia concept of 'tawakkul' (trust in God), emphasizing that spiritual alignment with the Divine command naturally subdues worldly distractions, contrasting with the chaos that befalls those enslaved by their ego (nafs).

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Qasim, from Abu Hamza, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic is Saying: “By My<sup>azwj</sup> Honour, and My<sup>azwj</sup> Majesty, and My<sup>azwj</sup> Magnificence, and My<sup>azwj</sup> Greatness, and My<sup>azwj</sup> Light, and My<sup>azwj</sup> Exaltedness, and the Loftiness of My<sup>azwj</sup> Position! A servant would not prefer his own personal desires over My<sup>azwj</sup> Desires except that I<sup>azwj</sup> will Scatter his affairs over him and Clothe his world upon him, and pre-occupy his heart with it, and would not Give him from it except what I<sup>azwj</sup> have Ordained for him.
And by My<sup>azwj</sup> Honour, and My<sup>azwj</sup> Majesty, and My<sup>azwj</sup> Magnificence, and My<sup>azwj</sup> Light, and My<sup>azwj</sup> Exaltedness, and the Loftiness of My<sup>azwj</sup> Position! No servant would prefer My<sup>azwj</sup> Desires above his own personal desires except that I<sup>azwj</sup> Make My<sup>azwj</sup> Angels to guard him, and the skies and the earth would guarantee his sustenance, and I<sup>saww</sup> would Back him from behind every trade with every trader, and the world would come to him and it (world) would be subdued’.
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Qasim from abu Hamza from abu la’ far (a.s.) who has said the following:

“The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has said, ‘By My Majesty, Glory, Greatness, Supremacy, My Light, Highness, and Exalted position, whoever of the servants gives preference to his desires over My wish, I make his affairs disintegrate, confuse his world upon him, make his heart grow preoccupied with it (desire) and will not give him more than what I have determined for him. By my Majesty, Glory, Greatness, My Light, Highness, and Exalted position, any servant who gives preference to My wish over his own desire, I will assign My angels for his security, make the skies and earth to guarantee his sustenance and I will be behind each one of his business deals with the merchants and the world will come to him subdued and compelled.”’
